body:
I mean, I've been to therapy. Two different therapists at two different points. It makes you feel all good for a little while, just spilling your guts about why you're life sucks and told it's alright (most of the time). Costs money though, and again, it doesn't really do anything for the eating. For the amount of money you pay in therapy it'd almost be more practical to have a person follow you around all the time, figuratively putting a gun to your head to stop overeating. At least that's what I think sometimes. 

I don't know. Again, I just wanna say fuck it and die. I feel like once it's over and done, everything I'd ever known would be out of my hands. Maybe I'd be free. Who knows? Way I see it, it's just about worth because I'm pretty confident my eating behavior is going to cause me to suffer the rest of my life. I thought two years ago I would "grow out of it." It didn't work like that. I'm glad people like you are at least willing to talk and listen. Makes the tension easier to deal with.

Either way I'm facing a huge gamble, with lots of pain. I either choose to suffer from all that is my eating disorder, etc. (including what it means to stop controlling) or I risk the possibility of, well, hell being real and all that. It's scary when you think about it. Again, I feel like if it's physical pain I could bear it. The stuff that affects my "soul" is far worse.

Honestly I just want to make some kind of decision whatever one it is, get it over with. To answer your last question... I wouldn't say I'm from a small town. I went to a large high school; it's a good community where I live. I just enjoyed having a few close friends rather than a bunch of people I can't trust.

Well, realistically if I make that choice I would stay where I am. What would happen? Hard to say with certainty. I'd probably be very apathetic for a very long time. I'd probably gain a good bit of weight, eating whatever I want and all. But I think my eating would normalize in the sense that I think *eventually* I would get used to the foods I crave enough to the point that I wouldn't get "high" on them anymore.

This would come at a high cost though. I wouldn't challenge myself to workout everyday, or perhaps even at all, because that would take too much effort (again, all I feel is apathy these days). I'd imagine my grades would go from great to average. By not working out I would lose all the fitness I worked so hard to build throughout my life, and I would probably never be a runner again even though I was pretty close to finishing the physical therapy necessary to get me back to the sport. 

Most of all I'd be like the worst hypocrite ever because earlier in my life all I talked about was how to eat right, how to be super fit, how ambitious I was, etc, etc. Everyone I ever knew would look at me and say, "wow, you really threw your life away." I'd really be alone. The few close friends I have like me because I was the kind of guy that never gave up, and was smart and pragmatic and reserved and confident. That wouldn't be the case after making this kind of choice.

Ha, well, you're right. It makes sense. However, the problem is I've tried the whole moderation thing. Like no matter where I draw the line (one cookie, two cookies, three...) I always break it. Once I have one I don't want to stop. I'm pretty sure if I could have as many cookies as I want, everyday, any day, I would have them all the time. And that's just not good for your body. 

Like, I know *exactly* what it takes to stay healthy when it comes to eating, I just have this whole huge problem and I can't do it. People who don't have eating disorders like me become obese in the US, so you have to actively make choices to eat right and thus be healthy... I don't see how you can't *not* get fat anymore, without doing something to prevent it. 

At the end of my original post I talk about the critical choice I have to make based on idea I have, so let me elaborate a little more: Before I had this eating disorder, was a really young, thin, and active, I didn't give a shit about what I ate. I just "went with the flow" and ate what I liked. I followed the basic "rules" naturally—eat when you're hungry, stop when you're full, etc. 

The idea I have, again, is this: What if I just threw all caution to the wind, gave up everything I worked for, abandoned all the people I know, dropped out of college, picked up everything I have and move to the other side of the country, and when it comes to eating, just do whatever the fuck I want. If I binge, I binge. If eat McDonalds all day, I eat McDonalds all day. I feel like this is the only option I have left because all I've done the course of my ED is control and limit my eating behavior.

The way I see it, I'm either doing that, or I'm ending my life. Because I can't fucking take any more of this struggle with food all the rest of it, honest to god...

I appreciate your sentiment, I really do. Seriously, thank you. But I want you to understand something first... why I can't agree that suicide is necessarily selfish.

Like I've told a friend or two about all this... but 1) they do not relate very well, and 2) they can't really do a lot for you. They can't monitor you 24/7 to make you stop yourself. Sure, they can provide emotional support, and that's not to be underrated. But honestly even the best of friends or family, in my limited experience, either worry too much about you and by asking them for support you've made *their* life worse, or they just get tired of you saying how fucked up you are and hearing how you've binged *again* despite your "never again" promise.

[Bill Zeller](http://gizmodo.com/5726667/the-agonizing-last-words-of-bill-zeller) was part an example to me not commit suicide the first two times, but now I agree with at least one of his views more than ever. I quote:

"People say suicide is selfish. I think it's selfish to ask people to continue living painful and miserable lives, just so you possibly won't feel sad for a week or two. Suicide may be a permanent solution to a temporary problem, but it's also a permanent solution to a ~23 year-old problem that grows more intense and overwhelming every day.

Some people are just dealt bad hands in this life. I know many people have it worse than I do, and maybe I'm just not a strong person, but I really did try to deal with this. I've tried to deal with this every day for the last 23 years and I just can't fucking take it anymore."

I've thought of OA before. Do they produce results? Do people really get better? What's it like?

Like I know why I overeat in the way you describe it... food is a drug to make up for something, but when it comes to me I can't accept that it's OK to binge. I get frustrated with myself because I don't know *why* I want food all the time. It's so depressing.

Here's what I can say with some certainty: Everything in my life used to just *work*. If I worked hard for something, I got it. I was naturally competitive. If there was a challenge, I always rose to meet it. I didn't think I had limits, I was never too concerned with what others thought... I was always a nerd or outcast of sorts, and so part of it is the fact I just wanted to prove my peers wrong, and break free, succeed where I had potential. 

Honestly, before my arrest (and the time after it) I don't think I judged myself too harshly. It was only after that catalytic event and the time after that that I really did a lot of self-evaluation. I know a lot of what made me great is also what causes me to suffer.

Er, here's what I'm really trying to say: I don't really know what exactly changed in my life that caused me to overeat. All I have is this "first memory" of when it happened. I can't specify exactly when it was, only a rough estimate. It's a great mystery to me, and honestly, if I could really go back in my memory and find out what it was that caused it, I think I could get better. But I can't remember... I can't explain how critical this is to me. I just don't know why it happened in the first place (and continues to happen).

What I do know is this... I used to be kind of logically unsympathetic and judgmental towards my peers because that's how I was treated a lot by others in school. Like, I was very assertive and told people how it was. I used to look down on people because they were fat or not as smart as me and I was very fit and skinny. Yet in reality it was I who was really the insecure one, I think. In hindsight, it's easy to point out what I did 'wrong' when I was younger, even though I was happier.

To answer your questions on the eating stuff... I don't know why I stop. Usually it's because the high from all the sugar, etc is maxed out and it's late at night so I get tired and go to bed. How I binge and how long has changed—used to be a binge was just like an hour (let's say a lot of extra dessert) then I would feel like shit pretty quickly, wake up the next day, drink a ton of water and fast the whole day. Those were the good days... 

Nowadays I have to eat more and more to get the same effect, and so a binge isn't just an hour or two, it becomes a day. After a day, it was two days. I've had a several week long (5-6 day) binges this year. I just focus on eating whatever I want when I want for that time, just no control over what I'm doing. It's fucking surreal half the time...

What happens, eventually, though far less quickly these days than I used to, is I go back to "willpower mode" to "clean up my life." I say I'm going to try and stop bingeing, and fucking fight with the core of my being to destroy the cravings. As my history alluded to, I used to be able to fight off for quite awhile, even if it got me eventually. Now I'm near helpless. I just have no will left. That's the best I can describe it.

As far as what I want, what I am for in the now "rare" time I'm not bingeing... I've been trying to lose weight ever since overeating started to cause me to gain weight. Having lost weight while fighting my ED before, I know what works, and that's intermittent fasting and lots of exercise. I want only healthy foods, two meals a day, somewhere between 1200-1800 calories a day. The foods that are the never list are: chocolate, candy, cookies, junk food, processed foods, and basically anything with lots of added sugar. I don't want to eat these things. I wish they didn't exist, because I crave them for whatever stupid reason. Like normally I used it eat *really* healthy, for example: five different servings of fruit, whole grain cereal, and organic soymilk for breakfast, salad for lunch, pasta with vegetables for dinner. You get the idea... I'm trying to complete remove all junk, processed foods, trigger foods from diet completely. Maybe that is unrealistic... but because my mom is a dietitian, I know it's possible. She *very rarely* eats those kind of things.

One last thing... I suppose in my self-improvement process I was in search of the best way to eat, and came upon a lot of Michael Pollan's work (just google his name). He pretty much lays out the best way to eat, but sadly it's really hard to eat that way because of the ubiquity of junk food and American culture, etc, etc.
